source.title: On Open Problems of Nonnegative Inverse Eigenvalues Problem

accepted.question_text: For a positive integer n, especially in the open range n >= 4 stated by the source, what are necessary and sufficient conditions for a multiset Lambda = {lambda_1, ..., lambda_n} of complex numbers to be exactly the spectrum, meaning the multiset of eigenvalues, of an n x n entrywise nonnegative matrix?

For a positive integer n, especially in the open range n >= 5 stated by the source, what are necessary and sufficient conditions for a multiset Lambda = {lambda_1, ..., lambda_n} of real numbers to be exactly the spectrum of an n x n entrywise nonnegative matrix?

For a positive integer n, what are necessary and sufficient conditions for a multiset Lambda = {lambda_1, ..., lambda_n} of real numbers to be exactly the spectrum of an n x n matrix that is both symmetric and entrywise nonnegative?
Given an n x n entrywise nonnegative matrix A, must there exist an n x n invertible real matrix P such that the similar matrix B = P^{-1} A P is also entrywise nonnegative?
Given an n x n entrywise nonnegative matrix A, must there exist an n x n invertible real matrix P such that the similar matrix B = P^{-1} A P is symmetric?
Given an n x n entrywise nonnegative matrix A, must there exist an n x n invertible real matrix P such that the similar matrix B = P^{-1} A P is both entrywise nonnegative and symmetric?
accepted.context_brief: similarity to a symmetric nonnegative matrix

evidence.quote: both non- negative matrix and symmetric matrix
